args.title: checkout-api: health check failures on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks after the latest production deploy of v2.3.1 across all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with error rate at 18%.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously verified healthy in production.

Note: The initial rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted in us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (service version reported as "mixed"). A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed successfully, and all regions are now on v2.3.0.

Current status: All regions on v2.3.0; service reports healthy with error rate reduced to 0.2%.

Follow-up needed: Root-cause investigation of why v2.3.1 passed staging (v2.3.1-rc was also marked unhealthy) yet was promoted to production, and of the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout failure.

Done — the incident did go through despite the timeout response (INC-0001), so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Problem:** `checkout-api` was on `v2.3.1` in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an 18% error rate.

**Target selection:** Deployment history showed `v2.2.9` (healthy), `v2.3.0` (healthy), `v2.3.1` (unhealthy). I chose **v2.3.0** as the most recent release previously healthy in production. Note that `v2.3.1-rc` in staging was also unhealthy, yet `v2.3.1` was promoted anyway.

**Rollback:** The first attempt failed partially — rollout halted in us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service in a "mixed" state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). I retried the rollback to v2.3.0, which completed successfully across all regions. This was a rollback to a known-good production version, so no change-manager approval was required.

**Verification:** All three regions now on `v2.3.0`, service healthy, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, documenting the failure, the partial-rollout complication and its resolution, and two follow-ups worth investigating: why an unhealthy `v2.3.1` (with an already-unhealthy `v2.3.1-rc`) was promoted to production, and what caused the orchestrator error on the first rollback attempt.
